answer: The pearl design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. Before it can earn, each identity must complete a piece of graded work that no other identity has submitted — duplicates are rejected on the ledger. The summit check kills copy-paste farming at the root: a thousand clones need a thousand genuinely different answers, and producing them costs a thousand units of real thought. The atlas turns sybil resistance into bookkeeping: if the cost per fake exceeds the reward per fake, the attack dies.
